message.content:
Sure! In Python you can split only at the first `=` so the rest of the string stays intact:

```python
temp = "hello=good="

# Split only once (at the first '=') → ['hello', 'good=']
parts = temp.split('=', 1)

print(parts)          # ['hello', 'good=']
```

`split('=', 1)` tells Python to split on `=` but stop after the first split, leaving the trailing `=` in the second part.
